manifest.title: Universal Eight-Axis Covenant Alignment System
manifest.pantheon_rule: The twenty-two attached Universal deity profiles are the only pantheon used.
manifest.class_rule: The attached twenty-two canonical merged classes each retain exactly one assigned deity.

best_features.use: The original four axes still produce one of the existing 81 names, preserving fast D&D-style shorthand without allowing the title to dictate behavior.
Every deity and class provides actionable duties and prohibited conduct instead of a vague moral label.
Characters declare values that can grant resolve when upheld at real cost and create complications when tested.
Convictions, duties, and relationships may be Minor, Major, or Defining rather than equally important.
Personal wants, class discipline, deity covenant, faction obligation, and relationships can conflict without being collapsed into one score.
Eight independent axes describe distinct patterns rather than treating goodness, obedience, mercy, reputation, and self-control as the same thing.
Violating a Defining Conviction creates Strain and forces reflection, repair, replacement, or deliberate abandonment.
What courts, temples, guilds, settlements, and companions believe is tracked separately from inner alignment.
Actions remain possible. The system records movement, covenant effects, reputation, and consequences instead of declaring that a character is forbidden to choose.
Players can see why scores moved, but repeated low-stakes behavior cannot farm alignment, favor, or XP.

axes.name: Altruism
axes.question: Whose welfare receives priority when interests conflict?
high_signals: accepting meaningful cost to protect others

axes.name: Lawfulness
axes.question: How does the character relate to laws, institutions, hierarchy, and stable procedure?

axes.name: Cooperation
axes.question: Does the character solve conflict through opposition and dominance or through coordination and shared authority?

axes.name: Honor
axes.question: How reliably does the character treat trust, truth, vows, surrender, and accountability?

axes.name: Mercy
axes.question: How does the character treat defeated, guilty, helpless, or dangerous beings when they possess power over them?

axes.name: Transformation
axes.question: Does the character preserve existing forms and continuity, or embrace alteration, reinvention, and becoming?

axes.name: Autonomy
axes.question: Does the character ground decisions in external duties and claims, or in self-authored conviction and consent?

axes.name: Restraint
axes.question: How strongly does the character regulate appetite, anger, fear, ambition, power, and impulse?

phases.name: Defining Low
phases.meaning: The low endpoint is an established part of identity and repeatedly appears under pressure.

phases.name: Contested Low
phases.meaning: The character leans low, but exceptions and internal conflict remain common.

phases.name: Pivot
phases.meaning: No demonstrated directional commitment. This is a precise center, not a personality absence.

phases.name: Contested High
phases.meaning: The character leans high, but the commitment is still tested, situational, or developing.

phases.name: Defining High
phases.meaning: The high endpoint is an established part of identity and repeatedly survives serious pressure.

starting_scores.deity_covenant_adjustment: 0-250 on up to three axes, chosen by the player from the deity's pressures
starting_scores.class_discipline_adjustment: 0-250 on up to two focus axes
starting_scores.creation_soft_limit: Normally 750-2250 unless established history clearly supports a defining phase.

profile_conversion.name_source: Only Altruism, Lawfulness, Cooperation, and Honor determine the existing 81 profile name.
profile_conversion.expression_line: Mercy, Transformation, Autonomy, and Restraint are appended as descriptors.

movement.rule: Movement records demonstrated behavior; it is not a reward or punishment.

convictions.slots: Two at creation; one may be Defining, one Major or Minor.

grades.major: A principle the character accepts meaningful cost to uphold.
grades.defining: A principle central enough to reshape identity, relationships, and major choices.

convictions.resolve: Accept a meaningful complication or cost caused by a Conviction, Duty, Tie, or Temptation to gain 1 Resolve, maximum 3. Spend 1 Resolve to add 1d6 after a d20 roll or to resist a deity Claim complication when the MOL allows.
convictions.strain: Freely violating a Major or Defining Conviction may add 1 Strain. At 3 Strain, repair it, rewrite it, abandon it openly, or fracture it into a Temptation.

ties.rule: Ties name people, communities, places, deities, factions, or ideals. They do not automatically set Altruism or Cooperation; the action taken because of the Tie determines movement.

reputation.rule: Only observers and institutions with knowledge of an action can react to it. Reputation never substitutes for inner alignment.

resonance.gain: Complete a deity edict or class bounty under meaningful stakes, normally no more than once per session.
resonance.loss: Freely violate an anathema or repeatedly embody the deity's shadow.

effects.0: Bounty triggers cannot restore Ichor; long-rest restoration and all permanent class features remain.
effects.1: The first successful bounty trigger after each long rest restores no Ichor unless paired with repair or atonement.
effects.2: Class functions normally, with no covenant bonus.
effects.3: Class functions normally and deity omens are clear enough to interpret.
effects.4: Once per long rest, fulfilling an edict at real cost grants 1 Resolve or restores 1 spent Bounty Ichor.
effects.5: Once per long rest, a valid bounty trigger may restore 2 Ichor instead of 1, never above maximum.
effects.6: Once per chapter, request a deity-specific miracle; accepting it increases Divine Claim by 1.

claim.gain: Accept direct miracles, bargains, shadow-driven power, or power beyond ordinary limits.
claim.loss: Resist divine pressure at meaningful cost, complete a severance rite, or choose autonomy when obedience would be easier.

effects.2: Recognizable omens and a deity-specific Temptation.
effects.3: The deity may offer a complication once per session; accepting it grants 1 Resolve.
effects.4: Miracles may demand a visible price or obligation.
effects.5: Refusing a direct demand requires spending 1 Resolve or accepting a serious narrative consequence.
effects.6: The character risks becoming an avatar, vessel, or living breach until the Claim is reduced.

class_influence.rule: A class supplies Practices, Hazards, focus axes, and an exact deity bounty. It never forces a score movement without demonstrated behavior.
class_influence.progression: At levels 1, 5, 11, and 17, choose or strengthen one Class Conviction. A multiclass character tracks one Duty for each class but uses only the covenant of the class whose deity grants the relevant feature.
class_influence.bounty: Completing a listed bounty trigger restores Bounty Ichor under the class rules. Under meaningful stakes it may also increase Resonance; it does not automatically move alignment unless the conduct itself demonstrates an axis.

anti_farming: No movement for filler dialogue or harmless repetition.
Normally one award per axis per scene unless separate consequential decisions occur.
Repeated conduct matters again only when stakes, cost, audience, or consequence changes.
A deity bounty cannot increase Resonance more than once per session unless a campaign-defining event justifies it.
The same creature, event, or object cannot be recycled to farm Ichor, alignment, Resolve, or Resonance.

metadata.merge_priority: The eight-axis alignment system is authoritative for rules; the 81-profile registry is authoritative for four-axis profile names and descriptions.

profile_registry.selection_rule: The four profile axes select one of these 81 readable titles; the remaining four axes form the expression line.

profiles.name: Lawful Renegade
profiles.description: A rebel in legal robes. They exploit loopholes, misrepresent motives, and use cooperative institutions for personal gain. Their planning may be pragmatic, but their low Honor comes from manipulating trust and abandoning principles when useful.

profiles.name: Lawful Drifter
profiles.description: Follows the rules just enough to survive. Doesn't stick around long, but won't burn bridges either. A ghost with a code.

profiles.name: Lawful Champion
profiles.description: Seeks glory under the banner of law. Noble in words, loyal to allies — yet always with an eye on personal legacy.

profiles.name: Lawful Strategist
profiles.description: A long-game planner who treats rules, promises, and people as pieces. They are disciplined and effective, but will deceive, sacrifice allies, or reinterpret obligations to secure their own advantage.

profiles.name: Lawful Knave
profiles.description: Keeps just enough law to stay out of jail. A slippery operator who toes the line without any deeper loyalties.

profiles.name: Lawful Avenger
profiles.description: Enforces personal justice like a holy wrathblade. Rules are tools, not ideals — they punish to feed their pride.

profiles.name: Lawful Mercenary
profiles.description: A sword for hire who respects the structure of a contract only while it benefits them. Precise and professional, yet willing to exploit clauses, conceal risks, or betray the spirit of an agreement.

profiles.name: Lawful Marauder
profiles.description: Wears structure like armor while carving a bloody path. Not cruel — just committed to their own violent climb.

profiles.name: Lawful Gladiator
profiles.description: Upholds combat as ceremony. Respects tradition and fair fights — but glory and personal honor always come first.

profiles.name: Neutral Renegade
profiles.description: Works with others when useful, then withholds truth or deserts commitments when the cost rises. Smart and efficient, but tolerated rather than trusted.

profiles.name: Neutral Drifter
profiles.description: A wanderer with just enough charm to stay welcome. Avoids attachment but doesn't actively sabotage it.

profiles.name: Neutral Champion
profiles.description: Fights for group causes — until the applause fades. Their heroism is real... but so is their thirst for praise.

profiles.name: Neutral Strategist
profiles.description: Judges everything by personal outcome. Plans quietly, manipulates information, and treats ethical limits as obstacles rather than commitments.

profiles.name: Neutral Knave
profiles.description: A wildcard with no compass. Acts on impulse or opportunity — sometimes helpful, often a headache.

profiles.name: Neutral Avenger
profiles.description: Revenge is their religion. Morality isn’t the goal — just evening the score, no matter who gets in the way.

profiles.name: Neutral Mercenary
profiles.description: Coin, leverage, and survival come first. They may honor a deal when convenient, but will switch sides, hide terms, or exploit weakness if the reward is better.

profiles.name: Neutral Marauder
profiles.description: Fights not for principle, but power. They don’t pick sides — only targets.

profiles.name: Neutral Gladiator
profiles.description: Honors the duel, not the war. Cares deeply about reputation and performance, not cause or creed.

profiles.name: Chaotic Renegade
profiles.description: A team-friendly anarchist until loyalty becomes inconvenient. They improvise brilliantly but lie, manipulate, or abandon allies without accepting the consequences.

profiles.name: Chaotic Drifter
profiles.description: A storm with a smile. Allies when it’s fun, disappears when it’s not. Hard to hate — but harder to trust.

profiles.name: Chaotic Champion
profiles.description: A rebel hero — dramatic, bold, magnetic. Loyal in the moment, but always the star of their own tale.

profiles.name: Chaotic Strategist
profiles.description: An unpredictable mastermind who plays every side. The dishonor lies not in improvisation, but in broken trust, concealed motives, and deliberate betrayal.

profiles.name: Chaotic Knave
profiles.description: Pure mischief incarnate. Chaos is its own reward — no loyalty, no plan, just vibes.

profiles.name: Chaotic Avenger
profiles.description: Burns worlds to avenge one wound. Justice isn’t blind — it’s furious.

profiles.name: Chaotic Mercenary
profiles.description: A volatile warrior for hire who treats promises as temporary. They may change sides mid-fight for better pay, greater thrill, or personal advantage.

profiles.name: Chaotic Marauder
profiles.description: Wrecks, raids, and rages with zero remorse. No ideology — just destruction.

profiles.name: Chaotic Gladiator
profiles.description: Fights like it’s performance art. Theatrics, blood, and brutal showdowns define them.

profiles.name: Lawful Operator
profiles.description: Works effectively inside institutions and teams, but manipulates procedure, hides costs, or uses allies as tools. Their public reliability masks a willingness to exploit trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Collaborator
profiles.description: A dependable participant in structured groups. They value order and teamwork, but are neither consistently self-sacrificing nor guided by a firm personal code. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Harmonizer
profiles.description: Builds stable institutions, resolves conflict fairly, and keeps commitments even when compromise is difficult. Order and cooperation matter more than personal glory. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Adapter
profiles.description: Uses rules and hierarchy as survival tools, changing loyalties or interpretations whenever advantage demands it. They respect structure more than they respect trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Moderate
profiles.description: Prefers order, proportion, and predictable procedure without strong altruistic or selfish pressure. Their personal code is situational rather than deeply fixed. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Ethicist
profiles.description: Supports structure while judging each duty against a consistent inner code. They are neither especially selfless nor selfish, but they are principled and accountable. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Ravager
profiles.description: Uses sanctioned force aggressively and treats legal authority as permission to intimidate, exploit surrender, or conceal misconduct. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Scoundrel
profiles.description: A disciplined bruiser who accepts hierarchy and conflict but follows no dependable moral code beyond the rules currently in force. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Warrior
profiles.description: Fights under rules of engagement, accepts consequences, and keeps their word. They may be confrontational, but their conduct remains principled. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Neutral Operator
profiles.description: A practical team player who gets results, but may hide costs, mislead partners, or discard commitments when efficiency demands it. Pragmatism alone is not dishonor; exploiting trust is.

profiles.name: Neutral Collaborator
profiles.description: Goes with the flow. A team member who supports without leading or resisting — blends in, stabilizes chaos.

profiles.name: Neutral Harmonizer
profiles.description: Balances relationships with grace. A quiet peacemaker, not for recognition, but because harmony matters.

profiles.name: Neutral Adapter
profiles.description: A survivalist who changes loyalties, stories, and standards to fit the moment. Flexibility becomes dishonor when they deny responsibility for promises made under earlier circumstances.

profiles.name: True Neutral
profiles.description: Stands at the living center of all four axes. Their choices are situational, mixed, and not yet consistent enough to establish a strong direction. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Neutral Ethicist
profiles.description: A quiet moral compass. Doesn’t preach, but always chooses the path that harms the fewest — even in stillness.

profiles.name: Neutral Ravager
profiles.description: Uses violence as a tool and ethical limits as optional. Efficient and undramatic, but willing to exploit surrender, conceal intent, or strike without regard for accepted restraints.

profiles.name: Neutral Scoundrel
profiles.description: A fighter without a cause. May brawl for coin, pride, or boredom — but rarely cares who wins the war.

profiles.name: Neutral Warrior
profiles.description: Wields strength as its own code. Neutral in belief, yet bound by a personal oath of fair combat and protection.

profiles.name: Chaotic Operator
profiles.description: Coordinates well through improvisation, but exploits goodwill, changes terms, or abandons shared commitments whenever freedom or advantage calls. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Collaborator
profiles.description: Works with others through spontaneity rather than structure. Helpful in the moment, but neither bound to a strong code nor driven by self-sacrifice. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Harmonizer
profiles.description: Creates community without relying on institutions. They keep their word, respect people over systems, and resolve conflict through flexible but principled means. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Adapter
profiles.description: Changes methods, identities, and loyalties rapidly, then denies obligations created by earlier choices. Their freedom is purchased with other people’s trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Free Spirit
profiles.description: Resists imposed structure and follows circumstance without a fixed altruistic, selfish, cooperative, combative, honorable, or dishonorable pattern. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Ethicist
profiles.description: Rejects external authority while following a steady personal code. Their principles are chosen rather than imposed, and they accept the consequences of living by them. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Ravager
profiles.description: Seeks confrontation without accepting restraint, accountability, or fair terms. Force and freedom matter more than promises or trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Scoundrel
profiles.description: Competitive, unpredictable, and quick to escalate. They are not reliably cruel or principled; the moment decides which side appears. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Chaotic Warrior
profiles.description: Fights freely and rejects imposed rules, yet respects chosen limits, worthy opponents, and promises made in their own name. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]

profiles.name: Lawful Coordinator
profiles.description: A mission-first organizer who brings order and aid to many, but cuts ethical corners, conceals costs, or sacrifices trust for results. Their altruism is genuine; their methods are not consistently honorable.

profiles.name: Lawful Mediator
profiles.description: A fair voice in the storm. Listens before acting, judges without ego, and restores peace without personal gain.

profiles.name: Lawful Guardian
profiles.description: The steadfast protector of the realm. Uplifts the weak, obeys the law, and inspires trust with every step.

profiles.name: Lawful Defender
profiles.description: Protects others through disciplined systems, yet may deceive wards, break promises, or use coercive shortcuts in the name of safety. The goal is selfless, while the method compromises integrity.

profiles.name: Lawful Arbiter
profiles.description: Seeks justice without bias. Mediates with detachment, but never loses sight of the greater good.

profiles.name: Lawful Sentinel
profiles.description: The silent watcher. Their loyalty is unwavering, their purpose pure — they serve to protect, not to be seen.

profiles.name: Lawful Enforcer
profiles.description: Uses sanctioned force to preserve public order, but abuses procedure, withholds truth, or violates surrender when expedient. They may serve others while still acting dishonorably.

profiles.name: Lawful Vigilante
profiles.description: Operates in shadows for the light. Defends the helpless but trusts fists over courts. A silent justice.

profiles.name: Lawful Crusader
profiles.description: A warrior of divine duty. Law and mercy guide their blade. Fights not for conquest — but for righteousness.

profiles.name: Neutral Coordinator
profiles.description: Helps where needed and solves problems quickly, but may manipulate allies, conceal tradeoffs, or break commitments to keep the work moving. Useful and altruistic, not always trustworthy.

profiles.name: Neutral Mediator
profiles.description: A calming presence. Bridges gaps between factions, friends, and foes alike. Emotionally grounded and peaceful.

profiles.name: Neutral Guardian
profiles.description: The quiet heart of the group. Protects without ego, speaks with compassion, and walks the path of kindness.

profiles.name: Neutral Defender
profiles.description: Prioritizes innocent lives over ideology, yet will lie, betray agreements, or use forbidden methods if convinced the outcome saves more people.

profiles.name: Neutral Arbiter
profiles.description: A watcher of balance and need. Neither law-bound nor wild, this figure serves the people — however that must look.

profiles.name: Neutral Sentinel
profiles.description: Honors a code of protection and patience. Acts when needed, guards without words, and never asks for praise.

profiles.name: Neutral Enforcer
profiles.description: Takes the blows so others do not have to, but uses intimidation, deception, and excessive force without a stable code. Selfless purpose does not erase dishonorable methods.

profiles.name: Neutral Vigilante
profiles.description: Stalks the wicked to defend the helpless. Walks the line between justice and vengeance.

profiles.name: Neutral Crusader
profiles.description: Champions the cause without borders. Fights for those who cannot, loyal only to their personal sense of good.

profiles.name: Chaotic Coordinator
profiles.description: Builds shelters, rallies communities, and overturns harmful systems, but may manipulate supporters or break promises whenever a new plan seems more effective.

profiles.name: Chaotic Mediator
profiles.description: The unconventional diplomat. Defuses tension with surprise hugs, strange jokes, or unexpected wisdom.

profiles.name: Chaotic Guardian
profiles.description: A wild protector with a golden heart. Thinks laws are optional, but kindness is sacred.

profiles.name: Chaotic Defender
profiles.description: Creates safety through unexpected means, yet may deceive allies, violate trust, or ignore agreed limits in the rush to save lives.

profiles.name: Chaotic Arbiter
profiles.description: A whimsical judge of right and wrong. Morals fluid, heart steady — they fight for people, not systems.

profiles.name: Chaotic Sentinel
profiles.description: Fights with passion and principle. Disregards rules — but never their personal honor.

profiles.name: Chaotic Enforcer
profiles.description: Tears down barriers for the oppressed, but uses coercion, humiliation, or broken promises as routine tools. The cause is compassionate; the conduct is dishonorable.

profiles.name: Chaotic Vigilante
profiles.description: A storm of justice. Protects others even when it means crossing lines, breaking rules, or being feared.

profiles.name: Chaotic Crusader
profiles.description: A freedom fighter wrapped in fire. Wields chaos in service of compassion. Unpredictable, unwavering.
